html:
São Tomé and Príncipe became independent from Portugal on 12 July 1975, after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon ended the dictatorship and its colonial wars.

Power passed to the Movement for the Liberation of São Tomé and Príncipe, which had worked from exile in Gabon. Its leader Manuel Pinto da Costa became president of a one-party state that seized the cocoa estates and leaned to the Soviet bloc. Most Portuguese planters left.

In 1990 a new constitution allowed rival parties, and in 1991 the country held free elections and saw the ruling party lose. It has since had several peaceful changes of power, unusual in the region, though it still depends on cocoa and aid. The memory of the Batepá massacre shaped its anti-colonial identity.
sum: São Tomé and Príncipe became independent from Portugal on 12 July 1975, after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon ended the dictatorship and its colonial wars.
